acceptance: One shared resolver (or a parity test across all three) for identity and phase
Throughput cohort identity includes or enforces a matching stream count
Phase names are normalized (case; standard maps to power)
SEED_CORPUS_SPEC.md documents which engines count as distinct identities
context: 2026-10-04 throughput adversarial review (#2382 branch 938150a4f and develop 8ed0c64e1).
description:
Three components define cohorts differently:
- Identity: scripts/generate_corpus_inventory.py:278-280 uses platform plus version for every cohort. The validator uses platform only, except under duckdb-version-matrix/. If the inventory were used for admission, three DuckDB versions would make a "3-identity" cohort (tpch@sf10.0 already lists 7 DuckDB versions).
- Phase: the explorer's _test_type (transformer.py:806-820) treats {"status":"NOT_RUN"} as executed, lowercases phases, and keeps unknown as its own cohort. The inventory and validator ignore NOT_RUN, don't lowercase, and merge unknown into power. Latent today: all bundles declare test_type.
- Uncommon test_type values (standard, combined, Throughput) each form their own cohort; standard is power-like (builder.py:779). This fails closed.
- Stream count is not part of throughput cohort identity, so 2-stream and 3-stream runs share a cohort.
- Same-engine padding: Spark SQL and PySpark both use pyspark; DuckLake and MotherDuck are DuckDB-based. No cohort currently relies on this to reach the floor.
